paragraphs: Kids in Cary love visiting us! With a playful, welcoming atmosphere and gentle, pain-free care, we make pediatric dentistry a fun and positive experience for children and teens.
Our experienced team of dental professionals is committed to providing exceptional care with the highest standards of clinical excellence and patient comfort.
Comprehensive dental care for every member of your family. From routine cleanings to advanced treatments, we provide exceptional care with the latest technology and techniques.
Our experienced team of dental professionals is committed to providing exceptional care with the highest standards of clinical excellence and patient comfort.

Located in Cary’s Crescent Green business park just off US-64 and Tryon Road, our Cary Family office provides easy access for patients across Cary, Apex, and Morrisville. The office is near Waverly Place shopping and convenient to US-1, making visits stress-free for children and their families.

We welcome families from across Wake County to enjoy Riccobene’s calming, compassionate approach. Whether you’re visiting from Lochmere, Regency, or surrounding neighborhoods, our Cary Family office is designed to make every dental appointment comfortable and convenient.
We believe in the Riccobene Way - a commitment to deliver better dentistry, better experiences and better results with a comprehensive and compassionate approach.
When you help a lot of people you get to some large numbers that we’re proud of - each satisfied patient is another happy smile.
Can't make it to our Cary office? We have other convenient locations in the area to serve you with the same exceptional dental care.
Quality dental care should be accessible to everyone. We offer flexible payment options, accept most insurance plans, and provide affordable membership plans for uninsured patients.
Save money on dental care with our affordable annual membership plans. No insurance? No problem! Get the care you need at a price you can afford.

Treating childhood dental needs, much like their medical needs, isn’t just a matter of providing the same care as adults require in a smaller mouth. Children are growing and developing, as are their mouth and teeth. We treat the unique needs of children as they mature in an environment designed for their comfort and staff who are expert at dealing with anxious, nervous, or animated during their appointment.

Thumb-sucking or pacifier use can cause dental issues if thumb-sucking or pacifier use persist past several years of age, particularly as permanent teeth begin to appear. Consult your dentist if you have concerns or questions about your child’s oral habits and experts can help you develop a plan to address their healthy dental development.

Regular brushing and flossing are the best way to prevent cavities at home, as well as starting and maintaining a regular dental care cadence as soon as your child’s teeth begin emerging. It’s never too early to establish good dental habits.

Both sealants and fluoride treatment are recommended to prevent cavities. Your dentist can explain the rule of fluoride to strengthen enamel and sealants to create a protective layer over areas of your child’s teeth that are prone to cavities and help you understand whether either sealants, fluoride, or both would be helpful for your child.

A child’s first dental visit should be as soon as practicable after teeth have begun emerging, ideally within six months of getting their first tooth. Establishing regular, routine dental care early in life sets the stage for a lifetime of smiles.
Take the first step towards optimal oral health. Contact our Cary office to schedule your appointment or ask any questions about our dental services.

Wissam Azzam, DDS
Dr. Wissam Azzam grew up in Long Island, NY, and earned his bachelor's degree in biology and chemistry from St. Joseph’s University. He attended NYU College of Dentistry, where he served as ASDA outreach chair and a teaching assistant, before completing his specialty training in pediatric dentistry at Stony Brook. Passionate about children’s oral health, he emphasizes minimally invasive care, fun visits, and healthy habits. Outside the office, Dr. Azzam enjoys time with family, hiking, weightlifting, and basketball, and is excited to serve local families.

FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS
How do pediatric dentists differ from general dentists?

Treating childhood dental needs, much like their medical needs, isn’t just a matter of providing the same care as adults require in a smaller mouth. Children are growing and developing, as are their mouth and teeth. We treat the unique needs of children as they mature in an environment designed for their comfort and staff who are expert at dealing with anxious, nervous, or animated during their appointment.

When should my child stop thumb-sucking or pacifier use?

Thumb-sucking or pacifier use can cause dental issues if thumb-sucking or pacifier use persist past several years of age, particularly as permanent teeth begin to appear. Consult your dentist if you have concerns or questions about your child’s oral habits and experts can help you develop a plan to address their healthy dental development.

What is the best way to prevent cavities at home?

Regular brushing and flossing are the best way to prevent cavities at home, as well as starting and maintaining a regular dental care cadence as soon as your child’s teeth begin emerging. It’s never too early to establish good dental habits.

Do kids need dental sealants and fluoride treatments?

Both sealants and fluoride treatment are recommended to prevent cavities. Your dentist can explain the rule of fluoride to strengthen enamel and sealants to create a protective layer over areas of your child’s teeth that are prone to cavities and help you understand whether either sealants, fluoride, or both would be helpful for your child.

When should I schedule my child’s first dental visit?

A child’s first dental visit should be as soon as practicable after teeth have begun emerging, ideally within six months of getting their first tooth. Establishing regular, routine dental care early in life sets the stage for a lifetime of smiles.
